Selection is carried out as per extant guidelines of the Competent Authority. The stages are as follows.

Screening of applications: Naval Dockyard Mumbai will not carry out detailed scrutiny of online applications before the examination. Detailed scrutiny of documents is done at a subsequent stage. Shortlisting: Fulfilling the basic criteria does not automatically entitle a candidate to the written examination. If applications are too many in proportion to vacancies
the authority may shortlist applications

in the ratio of 1:25 for every available vacancy in each trade and category. Merit calculation: Equal weightage (50:50) is given to marks in Class 10th from a recognised Board and marks in the ITI consolidated statement of marks for AITT issued by NCVET. For Crane Operator (SI)
100% weightage is given to Class 10th. For Rigger
100% weightage is given to Class 8th. Written examination: Objective type
OMR format
as described below. Medical examination: Selected candidates must submit a medical fitness certificate from a Government hospital before being engaged

as per Rule 4 and Schedule II of the Apprentices Rules. Document verification: Original documents uploaded on the portal are verified by Dockyard Apprentice School. Dates for verification and joining are intimated by email to selected candidates.
The written test has 100 questions of one mark each
is bilingual (English and Hindi)
and its questions match the Class 10th standard syllabus for all trades except Rigger
which follows the 8th standard syllabus. The exam is likely to be held on one day in one shift for all trades. Details of negative marking are not specified in the notification.
The exact date

time and venue are communicated to shortlisted candidates on registered email IDs and through the portal. The e-admit card must be downloaded from the portal. The exam is to be conducted in Mumbai and its suburban districts such as Thane
Kandivali etc.
Marks in the written examination are considered first. If written exam marks are the same
the older candidate (by date of birth) ranks higher. If date of birth is also the same
alphabetical order of the first name is considered.
PwBD candidates with disability of 40% and above: A scribe is given to candidates with blindness
locomotor disability (both arms affected – BA) and cerebral palsy if desired. For other benchmark disabilities

a certificate of physical limitation to write and need of a scribe is required from the Chief Medical Officer / Civil Surgeon / Medical Superintendent of a Government health care institution (Appendix I
MoSJE OM 34-02/2015-DD-III dated 29 Aug 2018). If the candidate brings their own scribe
the scribe's qualification must be one step below the candidate's

and details are submitted in the proforma at Appendix II of the same OM. PwD candidates with disability less than 40%: Scribe and/or compensatory time is granted only to those having difficulty in writing
on a certificate from the competent medical authority of a Government health care institution (Appendix I
MoSJE OM F. No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10 Aug 2022). Own-scribe rules are the same
with the proforma at Appendix II of that OM. PwBD candidates with medical categories other than blindness
locomotor disability (both arms affected – BA) and cerebral palsy
who need a scribe
must carry the relevant original medical certificate to the examination
failing which the scribe and compensatory time may not be allowed.

how_to_apply: Visit https://www.apprenticeshipregistration.com and download the online application guidelines before filling in the form.

Check that you meet the educational qualification and other criteria. Candidates from a Board or institution using the grade point system must get grade points converted into percentage of marks by the appropriate authority, or use a conversion chart from the respective Board. If unavailable, the lowest percentage of the grade point will be considered for shortlisting.
Keep your valid and active email ID and mobile number ready. No change in the email ID or mobile number is allowed once entered.
Write your Name and Date of Birth strictly as given in the matriculation certificate. Otherwise the candidature may be cancelled.
Upload the photograph, signature and documents listed above in the required formats and sizes.
Remember the password set during registration; further login is possible only with it.
Submit the application within the registration window and take a printout of the application form for personal record. No copy needs to be sent anywhere.
Download the E-admit card from the portal when released.

Candidates may apply for more than one designated trade in the same application. The examination centre for each may be one or different and may fall on the same day/shift. If two trades fall in the same shift, the candidate can appear for only one trade of his/her choice. If two exams are in different shifts on the same day, the candidate must reach the allotted centre.
important_instructions: Previous training: Candidates undergoing apprenticeship in any Govt./Public Sector/Private industrial organisation must terminate their ongoing contract through the MSDE Portal before applying, and must have fulfilled any cooling down criterion if applicable. Multiple applications: Do not submit multiple applications. If more than one is submitted, the one with the higher application number, if complete in all respects, is the only one considered. Provisional candidature: Applications are accepted provisionally. False or incorrect information leads to cancellation without prejudice to legal action. Caste certificates: SC/ST candidates must hold a latest caste certificate and produce the original on demand. OBC candidates must produce a valid caste certificate stating they do not belong to the creamy layer, in the format under GoI DoP&T OM 36033/1/2013-Estt(Res) dated 27 May 2013 and 36036/2/2013-Estt.(Res) dated 30 May 2014. If the OBC(NCL) certificate is not in the prescribed format or outside its validity period, the candidate is treated as General. Applying early: Apply well before the closing date. Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not responsible for mistakes in the online application or for non-receipt of communication on the registered mobile number/email. At the exam centre: Carry the admit card and an original photo ID (passport / Aadhaar / Driving licence / Govt. issued ID). Late reporting after the time on the admit card is not permitted. The name on the admit card is as per the matriculation certificate (Class VIIIth mark sheet for Rigger). If the name was changed and published in the official gazette after Class 10, a copy of the gazette must be given to the invigilator. Check the admit card for discrepancies before the exam; no correspondence is entertained after the examination. Exam conduct: Mobiles and electronic gadgets are banned in the premises, even in switch-off mode. Companions are not allowed at the venue or in its proximity. Candidates must arrange their own lodging/boarding and avoid bringing valuables. Results: Results of the written examination are published online through the portal. The option of opting out of personal information must be exercised at the time of filling up the online application. Hostel: Limited hostel facility for boys only, allocated on merit with first preference to outstation candidates; if vacant, it may be extended to local candidates (proof of current address required). There is no hostel or lodging facility for female candidates. Employment after training: Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not obliged to offer employment after training, and the apprentice is not obliged to accept. Ex-Naval Apprentices can apply for Tradesman Skilled in Naval Dockyards per recruitment rules, subject to the upper age limit for that post, which also applies to those applying for Tradesman Skilled in the Indian Navy. Updates: Check the portal regularly for updates, corrigendum and further instructions. Orders, circulars and formats of certificates are available on the portal under Reference Documents. Queries and grievances: Send queries to the help desk email [email protected] within seven days of uploading of the provisionally eligible merit list for written examination and the provisional select list. No queries are accepted after the seven days. The notification also prints Helpdesk Number 971842361.

Candidates found guilty of the following can be summarily cancelled at any stage of enrolment, apart from criminal action, and debarred from Naval Dockyard Mumbai examinations for the period below. The Naval Dockyard can also cancel candidature on any other ground it considers sufficient, or for any irregular or improper means.

The notification warns candidates to beware of touts and job racketeers who may falsely promise selection for illegal consideration. Selection is purely on merit, no money is required to be paid to anyone, and the written test and selection process are stated to be strictly on merit and transparent. For any grievance or assistance, candidates may email [email protected].

content_sections.heading: Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Age Limit
content_sections.text: As per the Apprentices Act, 1961, there is no upper age limit for apprenticeship training. Only a minimum age applies, counted on the crucial date (the closing date for receipt of online applications). Date of birth is taken from the Class X certificate issued by the concerned Education Board. If the date of birth is not mentioned there, the birth certificate issued by the Competent Authority is used. For the Rigger trade, if the candidate does not have a Class X certificate, the birth certificate issued by the Competent Authority is used. Note in the notification: an upper age limit is set in employment rules for the post of Tradesman Skilled in Naval Dockyards. It will apply to all ex-Naval Apprentices of Dockyard Apprentice School, Mumbai applying for that post after completing apprenticeship training. Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

content_sections.heading: Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Reservation Policy
content_sections.text: Reservation for SC and ST is as per Schedule II A of the Apprentice Rules, 1992, and for OBC (NCL) as per Maharashtra Act No. VIII of 2004. Reserved vacancies are filled separately from eligible SC, ST and OBC candidates, who are either lower in merit than the last candidate on the merit list of the UR category or SC/ST/OBC (NCL) candidates who have availed age relaxation, irrespective of their position in the merit list. Reserved vacancies for PwBD and ESM are filled from eligible candidates of the respective category who are lower in merit than the last candidate on the merit list of that category but otherwise found suitable for appointment even by relaxed standard. PwBD and ESM reservations are horizontal and cut across the vertical SC/ST/OBC(NCL) reservation (inter-locking reservation). Candidates selected against PwBD and ESM quota are placed in the appropriate category of UR/SC/ST/OBC(NCL), as the case may be. PwBD reservation follows MSDE-4/3/2023-AP(PMU) dated 11 Apr 25 regarding applicability of the RPwD Act 2016 to ATS and trade-wise suitability of PwBD. Persons with SD/SI with associated limb dysfunction are covered under the respective sub-category of LD, as the case may be. Horizontal reservation for Ex-Servicemen categories applies to the following, as per Para 3.6.3 of the Apprenticeship Training Manual: Children of deceased/disabled Ex-Servicemen including those killed/disabled during peace time Children of Ex-Servicemen Children of Serving Jawans Children of Serving Officers Ex-Servicemen Abbreviations used in the notification: UR – Unreserved; SC – Scheduled Caste; ST – Scheduled Tribes; OBC (NCL) – Other Backward Class (Non Creamy Layer); PwBD – Person with Benchmark Disabilities; ESM – Ex-Serviceman. Physical requirement suitability for PwBDs is as identified by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment notification No. 38-16-2020-DD-III dated 04 Jan 2021, amended vide notification No. 30-12/2020-DD-III dated 24 Aug 2022. Abbreviations: LD – Locomotor Disability; CP – Cerebral Palsy; LC – Leprosy Cured; DW – Dwarfism; AAV – Acid Attack Victims; B – Blindness; LV – Low Vision; D – Deaf; HH – Hard of Hearing; ASD (M, MoD) – Autism Spectrum Disorder (Mild, Moderate); ID – Intellectual Disability; SLD – Specific Learning Disability; MI – Mental Illness; MD – Multiple Disabilities; SD – Spinal Deformity; SI – Spinal Injury. PwBD candidates must hold a disability certificate issued by the Competent Authority, in the prescribed format under Rule 18(1) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Notification G.S.R 591(E) dated 15 Jun 2017, before applying online. The format is available on the portal under Important Documents. To avail reservation, the certificate must show 40% or above disability.

Submit the application within the registration window and take a printout of the application form for personal record. No copy needs to be sent anywhere. Download the E-admit card from the portal when released. Candidates may apply for more than one designated trade in the same application. The examination centre for each may be one or different and may fall on the same day/shift. If two trades fall in the same shift, the candidate can appear for only one trade of his/her choice. If two exams are in different shifts on the same day, the candidate must reach the allotted centre.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates
content_sections.text: Previous training: Candidates undergoing apprenticeship in any Govt./Public Sector/Private industrial organisation must terminate their ongoing contract through the MSDE Portal before applying, and must have fulfilled any cooling down criterion if applicable. Multiple applications: Do not submit multiple applications. If more than one is submitted, the one with the higher application number, if complete in all respects, is the only one considered. Provisional candidature: Applications are accepted provisionally. False or incorrect information leads to cancellation without prejudice to legal action. Caste certificates: SC/ST candidates must hold a latest caste certificate and produce the original on demand. OBC candidates must produce a valid caste certificate stating they do not belong to the creamy layer, in the format under GoI DoP&T OM 36033/1/2013-Estt(Res) dated 27 May 2013 and 36036/2/2013-Estt.(Res) dated 30 May 2014. If the OBC(NCL) certificate is not in the prescribed format or outside its validity period, the candidate is treated as General. Applying early: Apply well before the closing date. Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not responsible for mistakes in the online application or for non-receipt of communication on the registered mobile number/email. At the exam centre: Carry the admit card and an original photo ID (passport / Aadhaar / Driving licence / Govt. issued ID). Late reporting after the time on the admit card is not permitted. The name on the admit card is as per the matriculation certificate (Class VIIIth mark sheet for Rigger). If the name was changed and published in the official gazette after Class 10, a copy of the gazette must be given to the invigilator. Check the admit card for discrepancies before the exam; no correspondence is entertained after the examination. Exam conduct: Mobiles and electronic gadgets are banned in the premises, even in switch-off mode. Companions are not allowed at the venue or in its proximity. Candidates must arrange their own lodging/boarding and avoid bringing valuables. Results: Results of the written examination are published online through the portal. The option of opting out of personal information must be exercised at the time of filling up the online application. Hostel: Limited hostel facility for boys only, allocated on merit with first preference to outstation candidates; if vacant, it may be extended to local candidates (proof of current address required). There is no hostel or lodging facility for female candidates. Employment after training: Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not obliged to offer employment after training, and the apprentice is not obliged to accept. Ex-Naval Apprentices can apply for Tradesman Skilled in Naval Dockyards per recruitment rules, subject to the upper age limit for that post, which also applies to those applying for Tradesman Skilled in the Indian Navy. Updates: Check the portal regularly for updates, corrigendum and further instructions. Orders, circulars and forma

rows.type_of_malpractice: Seating at a place other than the designated place
Taking away examination material such as question paper, answer sheet, rough sheets, Naval Dockyard's copy of attendance sheet, or passing it to unauthorised persons
Making incorrect or false statements, suppressing material information, submitting fabricated, forged or tampered documents
Obtaining support or influence by irregular or improper means
Possession of a mobile phone in 'switched on' or 'switched off mode'
Misbehaving, intimidating or threatening examination functionaries (Supervisor, Invigilator, Security Guard or Naval Dockyard representatives)
Creating nuisance or disturbance at the exam centre, obstructing the examination or instigating others not to take it
A candidate who is also working on examination related matters in the same examination
Appearing in the exam with forged admit card, identity proof, etc.
Using unfair means such as copying from unauthorised sources (written material on paper or body parts)
Impersonation by or on behalf of the candidate
Possession of Bluetooth devices, spy cameras or other electronic gadgets in the examination hall
Taking snapshots or making videos of question papers or examination material, labs etc.
Sharing examination terminal through remote desktop software/Apps/LAN
Attempt to hack or manipulate examination servers, data and systems before, during or after the examination
Possession of fire arms/weapons during the examination

faq.question: Q1. What is the total number of vacancies for Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice (IT-28) Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are a total of 283 vacancies available for various apprentice trades under this recruitment notification released by Naval Dockyard Mumbai.

faq.question: Q2. When does the online application process start?
faq.answer: The online application registration process officially commences on 5 September 2026 for eligible candidates wishing to apply.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to submit the online application form?
faq.answer: The final date for submitting online applications is 27 October 2026. Candidates must complete their submissions before this deadline.

faq.question: Q4. What is the minimum educational qualification required for standard trades?
faq.answer: Candidates must have passed ITI (Consolidated all semesters) in respective trades under NCVT or SCVT with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit to apply for these apprentice posts?
faq.answer: The minimum age requirement for applicants is 14 years. Please review the official notification for additional details regarding upper age limits or relaxations.

faq.question: Q6. What is the monthly stipend provided for standard trades?
faq.answer: Candidates selected for standard trades will receive a monthly stipend of Rs. 9,600/- during their apprenticeship training period.

faq.question: Q7. How will candidates be selected for the apprenticeship training?
faq.answer: The selection process includes shortlisting based on qualifying exam marks in the ratio of 1:25, followed by a written examination and a medical examination.

faq.question: Q8. Is there any application fee required to apply?
faq.answer: No application fee is specified or required according to the official notification details for the Naval Dockyard Mumbai recruitment.

faq.question: Q9. Which official website should be used to register and apply online?
faq.answer: Candidates can visit the official registration portal at https://www.apprenticeshipregistration.com to complete their online application process seamlessly.

faq.question: Q10. What job type and location apply to this recruitment?
faq.answer: This is a contract-based apprenticeship opportunity located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, under the defence sector category managed by Naval Dockyard.
